ReviewProbe.Scope: Fresh independent read-only review of QR extraction caching, private correction buffers and pooled ownership, captured parent/enclosing deadlines, bounded QR/PDF417 cancellation polling and focused contracts. Previous DataBar and comparison/website contracts excluded.
ReviewProbe.ProductApiDisposition: Accept as shaped: internal engine ownership, public API and candidate priority preserved, no production dependency.
ReviewProbe.ReviewAllowance: One independent full pass; no targeted confirmation required.
ValidationGapsAtReview: Full frameworks and frozen corpus still pending.

FrozenQualificationBinary.Limit: The earlier focused host differs in commit metadata; this verifies its named contracts passed against the final measured core in the complete suite.

ReviewProbe.ValidationGapsAtReviewSettledBy: All three framework suites, exact tested/measured net10 core hash match and netstandard2.0 build. Frozen corpus and benchmark results are qualified separately.

ChangedDecoders: QR passes capture the enclosing monotonic deadline once and preserve the earliest parent deadline. Module extraction checks cancellation at most every 64 sampled modules; PDF417 grid sampling checks at most every 32 samples, matching its existing perspective sampler.

QR format candidates retain their existing order and correction/payload validation. The separately repeated both-copies-first subset pass is removed because the same comparator already orders those candidates first.

Broad QR fallback searches share immutable extracted bytes between candidates with the same mask. Every correction attempt receives private working bytes; cached and working pooled buffers are returned on success, failure and cancellation. Normal searches of eight or fewer candidates do not allocate the cache.
Codeword extraction and correction move into a semantic partial. No public API, production dependency, comparison hint, oracle, scoring rule, total timeout or recognition allowance changes.
AttributionLimits: This follow-up records 198/267 correct positive images versus 198/267 in the previous pass. Previously correct images lost: none; gained: none. Paired negative completion is [30, 29, 30, 29]/31 with the current binary and [30, 29, 30, 30]/31 with the previous qualified binary. All outcomes remain sensitive to shared-host contention and wall-clock budgets; no universal timeout or recognition advantage is established. QR extraction and deadline work reduce implementation cost without changing the total or family recognition allowances. Demonstrated regression gains do not establish accuracy on unseen photographs. Supplemental PDF417 images are regression evidence informed by prior remediation, not an unseen holdout. The invalid GS1 AI (3922) oracle and undeclared QR character encoding policies remain unchanged in scoring. Stacked DataBar and Expanded Stacked multiple-symbol localization and arbitrary perspective remain unproved; MaxiCode image scanning is unsupported.

RegressionProof.Coverage: Both erased QR format copies recover the exact payload, version, mask and correction level after earlier correction levels fail, for single-block and multi-block layouts. Cancellation during version40 extraction leaves the same symbol reusable. QR passes and tiles honor a shorter enclosing monotonic deadline, with local budgeting enabled or disabled. Existing scanner completion, PDF417 sampling/erasure and QR mask/encoding contracts remain qualified.
RegressionProof.HistoricalProof: Previous stacked DataBar qualification remains historical in previous-qualification.json and its retained archive. Current full suites, frozen corpus, supplemental images and timings are rerun.
RegressionProof.FocusedBinaryLimit: Focused experiments used a precommit diagnostic core. The complete final suites rerun those contracts against the frozen core used by the measurement host.

TestExecution.Net472: Task-local runner configuration disables collection parallelism; recognition allowances and assertions are unchanged.
TestExecution.Limit: Short wall-clock allowances remain sensitive to shared-host load. Serial legacy qualification is not proof for default parallel execution.
